title: Asking for clarification and interrupting politely

grammar.title: Domande indirette e softener (Could you tell me what…, I was wondering if…)
grammar.explanation: Nelle call le domande dirette ('What do you mean?', 'Why did it fail?') possono suonare brusche, soprattutto con un partner esterno. Le domande indirette le ammorbidiscono: si apre con una formula (Could you tell me…, Do you know…, Would you mind explaining…) e poi l'ordine diventa quello di una frase affermativa, cioè soggetto + verbo, senza do/does/did. 'Why did it fail?' diventa 'Could you tell me why it failed?'. Per le domande sì/no si usa if o whether: 'Is the file ready?' diventa 'Do you know if the file is ready?'. Altri softener utili: 'I was wondering if you could…' (richiesta molto cortese), 'Just to make sure I understand…' (verifica), 'Sorry to interrupt, but…' e 'Can I just jump in here?' (interrompere). Dopo 'Would you mind' il verbo va in -ing. Nota: 'I was wondering if…' è un'affermazione, quindi non serve il punto interrogativo.

examples.en: Could you tell me why the file was rejected?
Do you know if the custodian has sent the positions?
I was wondering if you could resend the file by noon.
Sorry to interrupt, but which environment are we talking about?
Just to make sure I understand, the API is being deprecated?
Would you mind explaining what you mean by 'soft limit'?

grammar.italianTrap: L'italiano non cambia l'ordine delle parole ('Mi può dire perché è fallito?'), quindi gli italiani dicono 'Could you tell me why did it fail?' o 'Do you know where is the file?'. Nella domanda indiretta l'ordine è affermativo: 'Could you tell me why it failed?', 'Do you know where the file is?'.

phrases.en: Sorry to interrupt, but can I ask a quick question?
phrases.it: Scusate se interrompo, posso fare una domanda veloce?

phrases.en: Can I just jump in here?
Before you move on, could I just add something?
phrases.it: Prima che passi oltre, posso aggiungere una cosa?

phrases.en: Sorry, I didn't quite catch that. Could you say it again?
phrases.it: Scusa, non ho capito bene. Puoi ripetere?

phrases.en: Could you tell me what you mean by 'pending'?
phrases.it: Mi puoi dire cosa intendi con 'pending'?

phrases.en: Would you mind going over the last point again?
Just to make sure I understand, you need the file by Thursday?
phrases.it: Per essere sicuro di aver capito: vi serve il file entro giovedì?

phrases.en: So, if I've got this right, the issue is on your side?
phrases.it: Quindi, se ho capito bene, il problema è da voi?

phrases.en: I was wondering if you could share the error logs.
phrases.it: Mi chiedevo se poteste condividere i log degli errori.

phrases.en: Could you slow down a little? The line isn't great.
phrases.it: Puoi andare un po' più piano? La linea non è buona.

phrases.en: Coming back to what you said earlier...
phrases.it: Tornando a quello che dicevi prima...

quiz.why: Domanda indiretta: ordine affermativo, soggetto + verbo ('the file is').

quiz.q: The partner bank's tech lead is talking fast and you've lost the thread. What do you say?
options: Stop, I don't understand anything you are saying.
Sorry to interrupt, but could you go back to the last point?
Excuse me, you speak too fast for me.
quiz.why: 'Sorry to interrupt, but…' + richiesta con 'could' è educato e preciso. Le altre suonano brusche o lamentose.

quiz.q: 'Do you know ___ the custodian has confirmed the positions?'
quiz.why: Domanda sì/no indiretta: si introduce con 'if' (o 'whether').

quiz.q: 'I was wondering if you ___ resend the corrected file.'
quiz.why: 'I was wondering if you could…' è la formula cortese fissa. 'Can' e 'will' non vogliono 'to'.

quiz.q: 'Why did the signature provider reject the document?' becomes 'Could you tell me why ___?'
options: did the signature provider reject the document
the signature provider did reject the document
the signature provider rejected the document
rejected the signature provider the document
quiz.why: Nella domanda indiretta sparisce 'did' e il verbo va al passato: 'why the signature provider rejected…'.

quiz.q: You want to confirm you understood the new cut-off correctly. Which is best?
options: What exactly did you say before about the cut-off time?
OK, it's clear, so the cut-off is changing then.
I don't really understand anything about this cut-off.
Just to check: the cut-off is now 4 p.m.?
quiz.why: Riformuli quello che hai capito e chiedi conferma: è il modo più rapido per verificare.

quiz.q: 'Would you mind ___ the error message in the chat?'
quiz.why: Dopo 'Would you mind' il verbo va sempre in -ing.

gapfill.text: Could you tell me what time the new cut-off ___?
gapfill.hint: ordine affermativo: il verbo va dopo il soggetto

gapfill.text: Sorry to ___, but which environment are we talking about?
Do you know ___ the vendor has deployed the patch?

reorder.answer: Could you tell me why the file failed?
I was wondering if you could share the logs.

fluency.prompt: The partner bank's tech lead says the file 'failed validation on our side'. You don't know which validation. Interrupt politely and ask. 25 seconds.
fluency.model: Sorry to interrupt, but could you tell me which validation failed? Was it the file format or the balances? Just to make sure we look in the right place.

fluency.prompt: The vendor's PM is speaking fast on a bad line and mentions a 'soft limit'. Ask them to slow down and explain the term. 30 seconds.
fluency.model: Sorry, I didn't quite catch that. Could you slow down a little? The line isn't great. And would you mind explaining what you mean by 'soft limit'?
keyPhrases: would you mind explaining what you mean

fluency.prompt: The KYC provider says document checks 'might take longer next week'. Use indirect questions to ask why, and whether it affects onboarding. 40 seconds.
fluency.model: Could you tell me why the checks might take longer? I was wondering if it's related to your new release. And do you know if it will affect clients who are onboarding right now?

fluency.prompt: In an internal call, a colleague is about to move on, but you want to add a point about monitoring. Jump in, check what you understood and make a suggestion. 40 seconds.
fluency.model: Before you move on, could I just add something? So, if I've got this right, we're keeping the old endpoint until March. I was wondering if we could add an alert on it, so we know when traffic drops to zero.
